- Model consistently underestimates prices, especially in early days of the forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to be too low in the first 5–10 days, then gradually rise — suggesting a lag in capturing near-term price momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., 79.80+), model forecasts overshoot and then fail to correct, leading to overestimation in subsequent days.
- Model shows weak mean reversion — fails to pull prices back toward historical averages after peaks.
- Forecasts are overly conservative in the first 10–15 days, then become more aggressive — possibly due to misjudging volatility or seasonality.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of price increases during the final 5–10 days of the forecast horizon.
- Forecasts often lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, especially in the first 10 days.
- Model exhibits a persistent downward bias in the last 5–10 days of the forecast, even when prices are rising.
